system_note: Audit of MR_09 - examiner reviewed the H&P, ED note, ICU progress notes, ID consult, nephrology consult, duplex imaging, procedure note, and discharge/transfer summary against the governing DRG policies for sepsis, septic shock, ARDS, acute respiratory failure, and VAP. Key points and citations: 1) Principal diagnosis and severe sepsis/septic shock (A40.3, R65.21): Admission documentation supports organism-identified sepsis (Streptococcus pneumoniae) with shock on presentation (ED lactate 5.1, hypotension, vasopressor start) and provider diagnosis of septic shock on admission. History & Physical (Admitting) documents septic shock secondary to community-acquired pneumonia and plans for vasopressors and broad antibiotics (History & Physical, p.312) and the ID consult documents admission blood cultures grew Streptococcus pneumoniae (Infectious Diseases Consult, p.137). Per the Sepsis policy, when organism-identified sepsis is present on admission, an A40.- organism-specific sepsis code is sequenced with R65.21 as an additional MCC when septic shock is documented. Evidence: H&P p.312; ID consult p.137. (ev1, ev2) 2) Acute respiratory failure (J96.01) and ARDS (J80): The H&P and ICU/consult notes document acute hypoxemic respiratory failure requiring intubation on admission (ABG/PaO2 58 on HFNC; emergent intubation) and provider-documented ARDS (H&P active problems and Nephrology/ICU notes showing very low P/F ratios (P/F 68) and bilateral opacities). These meet the J96.01 and J80 validation criteria (provider diagnosis, objective hypoxemia/P/F and imaging + risk factor sepsis). Evidence: H&P (PaO2 58 on HFNC / intubation) p.312; Nephrology consult (P/F 68, CXR compatible with ARDS) p.123; H&P active problem list includes ARDS, moderate-severe (p.312). (ev1, ev5) 3) Ventilator-associated pneumonia (J95.851) and organism coding (B96.5): ICU progress notes and the Infectious Diseases consult document suspected VAP on hospital day 6 with new right-sided consolidation and purulent secretions, and the discharge summary documents a hospital-acquired Pseudomonas pneumonia treated after bronchoscopy. The VAP policy requires provider documentation of VAP with timing >48 hours after intubation plus radiographic and clinical criteria; the record contains ID and ICU documentation meeting those criteria. POA=N for VAP is correct. Evidence: ICU progress note (VAP suspected, new right infiltrate) p.137; ID consult (day-6 VAP; admission blood cultures grew S. pneumoniae) p.137; Discharge Summary (hospital-acquired Pseudomonas pneumonia treated with cefepime after bronchoscopy) p.923. (ev4, ev3, ev6) 4) Acute kidney injury / dialysis dependence (N17.9, Z99.2): Admission labs show AKI with creatinine 3.1 mg/dL and nephrology documented indications for RRT; later the discharge summary documents renal recovery and dialysis discontinued. The AKI code and a POA=Y / dialysis-dependence coded as occurring during stay (POA=N) are consistent with documentation. Evidence: H&P labs (Cr 3.1 mg/dL) p.312; Nephrology consult indicating RRT initiation p.123; Discharge summary noting dialysis discontinued p.923. (ev1, ev5, ev6) 5) Incorrect laterality on catheter-associated IJ DVT (I82.C12 billed): Multiple bedside/diagnostic notes document a catheter-associated RIGHT internal jugular DVT (venous duplex and the discharge summary), whereas the claim line billed left IJ thrombosis (I82.C12). The clinical record consistently documents right IJ DVT; coding the left-sided code is incorrect. Action: recode I82.C12 -> I82.C11 (right internal jugular DVT). Evidence: Venous duplex / progress note documenting right IJ DVT p.330; Discharge / Transfer Summary documenting catheter-associated right IJ DVT p.923. (ev7, ev6) 6) Tracheostomy technique mismatch (0B110F4 billed as open approach): The procedure note documents a bronchoscopically guided percutaneous dilational tracheostomy (serial dilation) with immediate capnographic confirmation and no pneumothorax. The billed code is for an open approach tracheostomy; per the record the approach was percutaneous dilational. Action: the billed open-approach tracheostomy code (0B110F4) is not supported and must be removed/replaced with the appropriate percutaneous tracheostomy ICD-10-PCS code. Evidence: Procedure Note - Percutaneous Dilational Tracheostomy (bronchoscopically guided percutaneous dilational tracheostomy) p.468. (ev8) Summary determination and immediate corrections required: - Finding: coding errors requiring correction: 1) laterality error on IJ DVT (left -> right); 2) procedure approach for tracheostomy coded as open surgery but documentation supports percutaneous dilational technique (billed 0B110F4 unsupported). Other billed diagnoses (A40.3, R65.21, J96.01, J80, J95.851, N17.9, etc.) are supported by provider documentation and meet policy validation criteria (supporting POA flags as recorded). Citations: History & Physical (Admitting) p.312; Infectious Diseases Consult p.137; ICU progress notes p.137; Nephrology consult p.123; Venous duplex / Progress note p.330; Procedure Note (Percutaneous Dilational Tracheostomy) p.468; Discharge / Transfer Summary p.923. (ev1, ev2, ev4, ev5, ev7, ev8, ev6) Note: the exact ICD-10-PCS code for percutaneous dilational tracheostomy is not unambiguously determined from the retrieved claim/lookup rows here. I have removed the unsupported open-approach tracheostomy (0B110F4) from the corrected procedure list below and flagged this for human confirmation of the precise percutaneous PCS code to add. See HITL question.
rationale_letter: Re: Clinical Coding Audit - MR_09 (Admission 04/04/2026) Dear Provider/Health Information Management Team, We completed a DRG-focused audit of the hospital stay for MR_09. The review compared the billed diagnosis and procedure set to the medical record and the applicable DRG coding policies. Based on the medical record and governing policy, we have identified coding findings that require correction. Finding and Basis: 1) Incorrect laterality: The claim billed I82.C12 (acute embolism and thrombosis of left internal jugular vein). Diagnostic imaging and clinical documentation consistently record a catheter-associated right internal jugular DVT (venous duplex and discharge summary). Evidence: Venous duplex / Progress Note (right internal jugular deep vein thrombosis) and Discharge / Transfer Summary ("catheter-associated right IJ DVT") (medical record pages cited). Therefore the code should be corrected to the right-sided code (I82.C11) to reflect the documented laterality. 2) Procedure technique miscoding - tracheostomy: The claim includes ICD-10-PCS 0B110F4 (bypass trachea to cutaneous with tracheostomy device, open approach). The procedure note documents a bronchoscopically guided percutaneous dilational tracheostomy (serial dilation) with tube placement and immediate capnographic confirmation and no pneumothorax. The medical record therefore does not support an open-approach tracheostomy code. The open-approach PCS code must be removed and replaced by the ICD-10-PCS code that specifically represents a percutaneous dilational tracheostomy. Evidence: Procedure Note - Percutaneous Dilational Tracheostomy (bronchoscopically guided percutaneous dilational tracheostomy) p.468. Other supported documentation (no change recommended): Provider documentation supports organism-identified sepsis due to Streptococcus pneumoniae on admission (A40.3), severe sepsis with septic shock (R65.21), acute hypoxemic respiratory failure (J96.01), ARDS (J80), ventilator-associated pneumonia later in the admission (J95.851, POA=N) with Pseudomonas identified as the causative organism (supporting B96.5 as secondary organism code). AKI requiring RRT is documented (N17.9) with renal recovery documented at discharge. These codes meet the policy validation criteria cited (Sepsis/Septic Shock, ARDS, Acute Respiratory Failure, VAP policies). Correction being made: - Recode I82.C12 (left IJ) -> I82.C11 (right IJ) based on duplex and discharge documentation. - Remove unsupported procedure 0B110F4 (tracheostomy, open approach) and replace with the correct percutaneous tracheostomy ICD-10-PCS code (to be confirmed; see HITL request below). Requested action / next step: - Please confirm and supply the correct ICD-10-PCS code for the documented bronchoscopically guided percutaneous dilational tracheostomy so the claim can be updated to reflect the correct technique. If you have additional documentation that contradicts the findings above (for example, a different procedure note or operative report describing an open tracheostomy or an explicit left-sided IJ thrombus), please provide it for reconsideration. Sincerely, Clinical Claims Auditor
